measuring-length-skill-01.target: I can measure the length of an object to the nearest inch or centimeter with a ruler.
measuring-length-skill-01.ifCorrect: You can do this: can measure the length of an object to the nearest inch or centimeter with a ruler.
measuring-length-skill-01.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Starting at 1 instead of 0, or counting the tick marks instead of the spaces. Try this: Line up the end of the object with 0 and count the units (spaces) it covers.

measuring-length-skill-02.skill: Choosing a Measuring Tool and Unit
measuring-length-skill-02.target: I can choose a ruler, yardstick, meter stick, or measuring tape and the best unit for the length I need to measure.
measuring-length-skill-02.ifCorrect: You can do this: can choose a ruler, yardstick, meter stick, or measuring tape and the best unit for the length I need to measure.
measuring-length-skill-02.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Choosing the tool with the biggest numbers, or measuring a long hallway in centimeters with a short ruler. Try this: Compare how many times the tool would need to be moved; choose the tool that fits the object.

measuring-length-skill-03.target: I can measure an object with two units and explain why a smaller unit gives a bigger number.
measuring-length-skill-03.ifCorrect: You can do this: can measure an object with two units and explain why a smaller unit gives a bigger number.
measuring-length-skill-03.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Thinking a larger number always means a longer object, even when the units are different. Try this: Measure the same desk with paper clips and with pencils and compare the counts.

measuring-length-skill-04.target: I can estimate lengths in inches, feet, centimeters, and meters using benchmarks.
measuring-length-skill-04.ifCorrect: You can do this: can estimate lengths in inches, feet, centimeters, and meters using benchmarks.
measuring-length-skill-04.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Mixing up the size of the units (a door is 2 inches tall). Try this: Use body benchmarks: a fingertip is about 1 centimeter, a paper clip about 1 inch, a long step about 1 meter.

measuring-length-skill-05.target: I can measure two objects and find how much longer one is than the other.
measuring-length-skill-05.ifCorrect: You can do this: can measure two objects and find how much longer one is than the other.
measuring-length-skill-05.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Adding the two lengths, or comparing measurements that use different units. Try this: Line up the objects at 0 and find the difference by counting up from the shorter length.

measuring-length-skill-06.target: I can measure several objects to the nearest whole unit and show the data on a line plot.
measuring-length-skill-06.ifCorrect: You can do this: can measure several objects to the nearest whole unit and show the data on a line plot.
measuring-length-skill-06.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Putting every X at a different place, or reading the number of X marks as the length. Try this: Build the line plot from a tally of the measurements; each X is one object.
